## Root-cause status 2026-10-27 ~22:15 PDT — the writer is still unidentified, and here is exactly what was checked

The ticket records `uv self update` as **inferred, not observed**. That remains true after today's checks. What I can now add is the negative evidence, so the next investigator does not repeat it.

### Checked, and silent

- **The pin directory holds no installer metadata.** `~/.local/share/uv-pins/` contains only `0.12.7/`, and that directory contains only `uv`, `uv.0.13.6.bak` and `uvx`. There is **no `uv-receipt.json`** — the file `uv self update` writes to record an install. Its absence means the pin directory was never populated by uv's own installer, so `uv self update` had no receipt to consult. That is evidence *against* a clean self-update and *for* a binary dropped in by hand or by a copy.
- **Current state is correct and the displaced binary is preserved.** `~/.local/share/uv-pins/0.12.7/uv` reports `uv 0.12.7 (61291a8ca 2026-08-27 aarch64-apple-darwin)`; `uv.0.13.6.bak` (27.7 MB) sits beside it. Both are dated Oct 27 04:38.
- **Homebrew is a live 0.13.x source on this host.** `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv` is a symlink to `../Cellar/uv/0.13.5/bin/uv`, dated Oct 24 16:50. That is **0.13.5**, not the 0.13.6 that appeared in the pin directory, so a `brew upgrade uv` does not explain the swapped binary by itself — but it does establish that this host carries a second, moving uv installation on `PATH` behind the pin.
- **`PATH` order is correct.** `which -a uv` resolves `~/.local/share/uv-pins/0.12.7/uv` before `/opt/homebrew/bin/uv`, so the pin wins today.
- **No shell history or installer log was inspected.** Still true, and still the gap.

### Why this matters for the already-decided fix

The operator decision — `make venv` verifies the pinned uv against `[tool.uv] required-version` and, on mismatch, fetches the required release into a **version-keyed, checksum-verified cache under the repo's own cache directory**, never modifying what is on `PATH` — is unaffected by the writer remaining unknown, and is the right call precisely *because* it is unknown. A repair that writes into `~/.local/share/uv-pins/` would be writing into a host convention the repo does not own and cannot defend against the next rewrite; a repo-owned cache is immune to whatever did this.

### Related, and likely the same class

Bug `degraded-chilly-galago` (`bb19-4776-46d2-4223`) is the same defect shape: a pinned artifact whose contents are not what the pin claims — there, `pypandoc_binary` 1.17's arm64 wheel shipping an x86_64 pandoc (confirmed unfixed upstream, [pypandoc#447](https://github.com/JessicaTegner/pypandoc/issues/447), and 1.17 is the newest release). Both want the same bootstrap behaviour: **verify the artifact, not its label, and repair into a repo-owned checksum-verified cache.** They should share one mechanism rather than growing two — which also keeps `check_mechanism_delta` satisfied, since two independent bootstrap-repair mechanisms would be two new census entries.

### Not done

No code was written for this ticket in this session. The ticket stays `in_progress` with its PASS attestation current.

### Explicitly unproven

What rewrote the binary. `uv self update` is now *less* likely than when this was filed, because the pin directory has no uv receipt; a file copy or an unpacked archive fits the evidence at least as well. Shell history, `~/.cache/uv/`, and any wrapper script on this host remain unexamined.
